name: The Unruh Effect
statement: The Unruh effect predicts that a uniformly accelerating observer in vacuum perceives a thermal bath of particles at a temperature set by their acceleration.
statementAccent: perceives a thermal bath of particles
meaning: The Unruh effect is a theoretical prediction of quantum field theory that the particle content of a field is observer-dependent: what an inertial observer sees as empty vacuum, a uniformly accelerating observer instead perceives as a warm thermal bath of particles. The predicted Unruh temperature is proportional to the observer’s proper acceleration.
mechanism: An accelerating observer’s worldline is naturally described using Rindler coordinates, bounded by a causal horizon; quantising the field using Rindler modes instead of Minkowski modes requires a Bogoliubov transformation that mixes creation and annihilation operators, so the Minkowski vacuum appears, from the accelerated observer’s perspective, as a thermal state populated with Rindler particles.

examples.text: The Unruh temperature formula has the same mathematical form as the Hawking temperature of black-hole radiation, linking the two via the equivalence principle and giving rise to the term "Hawking–Unruh effect."

The 2019 NA63 experiment at CERN, using channelling radiation from electrons undergoing extreme acceleration in a crystal, was proposed as possible indirect evidence, though whether it demonstrates the effect remains disputed.

Theoretical proposals describe schemes using an accelerated extended atomic system as an "Unruh–DeWitt detector," since the accelerations needed in simple point-particle setups are far beyond current laboratory reach.

whyItMatters: The Unruh effect reveals a deep, observer-dependent feature of quantum field theory and forges a conceptual bridge between quantum mechanics, acceleration, and black-hole/horizon thermodynamics, informing ongoing research into quantum gravity.
limits: The predicted temperature is minuscule for any achievable acceleration, Earth’s surface gravity corresponds to roughly 4×10⁻²⁰ K, placing direct detection far beyond current experimental capability; it has not yet been unambiguously, directly confirmed in the laboratory.
misreadings: It is often conflated with Hawking radiation itself; although mathematically analogous, the Unruh effect arises from acceleration in flat spacetime while Hawking radiation arises from spacetime curvature near a black-hole horizon: related but physically distinct. Claims that it has already been observed are actively disputed.
origin: Anticipated by Stephen Fulling (1973) and Paul Davies (1975), and given its standard form by William G. Unruh in his 1976 paper "Notes on Black Hole Evaporation."

sources.text: Unruh effect, Wikipedia. — the definition, the Unruh temperature, the Rindler-horizon mechanism, the Fulling/Davies/Unruh history, and the disputed NA63 claim.
William Unruh, Wikipedia. — his 1976 Physical Review D paper as the formal origin of the effect.
